body: Making machine learning challenges legible: one picture per problem, for competitions run at NeurIPS, CVPR, ICCV, ISMIR and the KDD Cup.

AIcrowd runs open machine learning challenges. Our work with them is the longest technical design relationship in the studio's history: our CEO, Rabiul Islam, started it years before Studio 1947 formally existed, and the studio now carries it. When AI researchers and enterprise data teams look for a creative partner they do not want a traditional graphic agency; they need someone comfortable with abstract maths, clear communication and data visualisation.

sections.heading: The problem
body: A challenge arrives as a paragraph of research language and a dataset. It has to leave as something a person will stop scrolling for, without misrepresenting the science underneath it.

cards.title: Rule
cards.body: The picture carries the problem rather than decorating it. No stock circuit boards, no glowing brains, no blue hexagons. Where a field already has an object that means something to its people, the design uses that object.

cards.title: Method
cards.body: The clock a clinician asks a patient to draw; the dataset's own column names; the pose skeleton a researcher sees in their annotations. Recognition does the work a headline cannot.

cards.title: Series
cards.body: For multi-part events, one scene held constant and one element changed per task, so five puzzles read as five parts of one thing.

body: Almost none of these were AIcrowd's alone. A challenge is run with the group that owns the problem and the data, and the work was made at AIcrowd for them: the Alzheimer's Disease Data Initiative on clock drawings, OpenAI on generalisation, Amazon on shopping queries, ZEW on data purchasing, Meta on multi-modal retrieval. Whose challenge it is decides the register the picture is allowed to use, which is why the Alzheimer's banner refuses to be excited about itself. Each panel below names both.

sections.heading: The work, one at a time
body: The set below runs in order, each with a note on what that particular problem was and why it was drawn the way it was.

media.alt: NeurIPS 2020 Procgen Competition key visual: retro 8-bit game environments rebuilt as clean modular vector tiles

body: Made at AIcrowd · Made for OpenAI · Concept & design Rabi · Open on AIcrowd

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: The subject has no natural picture, so the picture is ascent. Sixteen procedurally generated worlds, each a real frame from the benchmark, are stacked into a rising staircase and the agent climbs it, so the sample efficiency and the generalisation named in the subhead are the same movement upward. The frames are shown as themselves rather than stylised, because a researcher recognises the environments and that recognition is the fastest way to say this challenge is yours. OpenAI's mark sits beside AIcrowd's at the same weight.

cards.title: Science communication
cards.body: Procgen asks a narrow, difficult question: can an agent that has mastered some levels of a game handle levels it has never seen? The subject is generalisation.

media.alt: NeurIPS 2021 AWS DeepRacer key visual: velocity lines, racing track grids and telemetry indicators

sections.subheading: NeurIPS 2021: AWS DeepRacer AI Driving Olympics
body: Made at AIcrowd · Made for Amazon Web Services · Concept & design Rabi

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: The image is one continuous road that begins as a wireframe mesh, the way a simulator renders ground, and then lifts off that mesh and curls upward into open space, solid and lit, with the car at the point of transition. Nothing else moves. Sim-to-real is usually explained in a paragraph; here it is one line going up off its own grid.

cards.title: Science communication
cards.body: The hard part of this challenge is the sim-to-real gap: a policy is trained in simulation and then has to drive a physical car on a physical track, where friction and light and tyre wear are all real.

media.alt: Multi-Agent Behavior Challenge 2022 key visual, intersecting neon motion trajectories forming behavioural clusters

body: Made at AIcrowd · Made for Northwestern, Google, Amazon and Janelia · Concept & design Rabi

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: The mice and the flies here are not drawn and then covered in dots: they are built out of the keypoints, so each animal exists only as the tracked points a model would ever receive, and the eye assembles the creature the way the model has to. It is as close as a still image gets to showing the machine's view rather than ours. Northwestern, Google, Amazon and Janelia across the top.

cards.title: Science communication
cards.body: Learning behavioural representations from animal poses in video: the dataset is footage of interacting animals annotated frame by frame, and the task is to represent and classify what they are doing.

media.alt: Data Purchasing Challenge 2022 key visual: geometric arrays and dark-mode data nodes evoking an algorithmic trading floor

body: Made at AIcrowd · Made for ZEW, Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research · Concept & design Rabi

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: The image is a balance, tipped. A purse sits on one pan and on the other a spray of unlabelled points fans up and falls back into the dish, the quantity you might buy. What is being weighed is money against information, and a scale states that trade in the second the picture gets before someone scrolls past.

cards.title: Science communication
cards.body: This one is an economics problem wearing machine learning clothes: given a fixed budget, which unlabelled data should you pay to have labelled? Nothing about model architecture will answer it.

media.alt: ADDI Alzheimer's Detection Challenge key visual, organic neural pathway composition over a typographic grid

body: Made at AIcrowd · Made for Alzheimer's Disease Data Initiative · Concept & design Rabi · Open on AIcrowd

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: The banner refuses the usual brain scan and uses the instrument itself. A clock face disperses into particles from the right, and beneath it a line of figures walks left to right through a whole life, child to stooped elder with a stick, the last of them already inside the dispersal. Two things are being lost at once and they are drawn as one event. The prize list underneath is deliberately plain: this is a medical problem and the design should not be excited about it.

cards.title: Science communication
cards.body: Early Alzheimer's is screened with the clock-drawing test: a patient is asked to draw a clock showing a given time, and what a clinician reads is not the clock but the way the drawing fails. Numbers crowd into one quadrant, hands go missing, the circle does not close.

media.alt: SUADD '23 key visual: vector tracking grids, bounding boxes and depth heatmaps over an aerial landscape

sections.subheading: Scene Understanding for Autonomous Drone Delivery (SUADD '23)
body: Made at AIcrowd · Concept & design Rabi

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: We made machine vision itself the key visual. We laid bright vector tracking grids, bounding boxes and pixel-level depth heatmaps over scenic aerial landscapes. Developers scanning the page could see the exact goal of the computer vision model straight away.

cards.title: Science communication
cards.body: Computer vision models trained for real-time semantic segmentation, depth estimation and obstacle avoidance in flight routing.

media.alt: Amazon KDD Cup 2024 challenge key visual: network-graph artwork mapping multi-task LLM commerce tracks

sections.subheading: Amazon KDD Cup 2024: Multi-Task Online Shopping for LLMs
body: Made at AIcrowd · Made for Amazon · Concept & design Rabi

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: No single object depicts four jobs at once, so the composition splits the work between subject and ground. The subject is a shopping bag whose handle is Amazon's own arrow, whose body is a knowledge graph of connected nodes, and whose tab is a search field, with the assistant standing inside it as though the bag were the shop. The ground is the tasks themselves, drawn faintly and evenly across the field.

cards.title: Science communication
cards.body: The word carrying this title is multi-task: one language model has to answer product questions, rank results, reason about a basket and hold a conversation, all inside the same shop.

media.alt: Sounding Video Generation Challenge 2024 key visual, audio frequency spectrograms blended into cinematic video strips

body: Made at AIcrowd · Concept & design Rabi

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: A masterclass in cross-modal visualisation. We built a striking grid system that blends audio frequency spectrograms with cinematic video strip layouts. The design maps how sound waves rise directly out of motion. It gives generative media researchers a beautiful, harmonious challenge interface.

cards.title: Science communication
cards.body: Generative models that analyse video feeds and produce matching high-fidelity spatial audio, perfectly in sync with the visual timeline.

media.alt: Global Chess Challenge 2025 key visual: chessboard reimagined as a matrix field with minimalist vector piece nodes

body: Made at AIcrowd · Concept & design Rabi

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: We completely reimagined the traditional chessboard as a mathematical matrix field. Physical chess pieces became minimal vector nodes projecting calculated paths. The creative direction linked timeless human strategy with the depth of modern AI processing.

cards.title: Science communication
cards.body: Deep-learning neural networks trained to evaluate non-traditional board structures, graph networks and complex predictive game trees.

media.alt: Commonsense Persona-Grounded Dialogue Challenge 2025 key visual, typographic thought clouds over semantic matching matrices

body: Made at AIcrowd · Concept & design Rabi

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: Showing human personality through code takes several abstract layers. We built a system of overlapping typographic thought clouds and semantic matching matrices. It shows how an algorithm weighs context, empathy and logic while generating text in conversation with a person.

cards.title: Science communication
cards.body: Pushing conversational NLP engines to keep logical consistency, common-sense reasoning and careful persona tracking across multi-turn dialogues.

media.alt: Meta CRAG Multi-Modal Challenge 2025 key visual, dark-mode data fusion of video, image and speech into one retrieval pipeline

body: Made at AIcrowd · Made for Meta · Concept & design Rabi

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: Working within strict institutional rules, we built a premium, dark-mode visual framework for data fusion. It shows separate raw media formats dissolving into a single, high-performance retrieval pipeline. The result is a polished visual presence that matches Meta's engineering standards.

cards.title: Science communication
cards.body: Taking Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) further by asking engineers to fuse real-time web text with complex video, image and speech inputs, under Meta's technical guidelines.

sections.heading: What this taught the studio
body: Our long-running work with AIcrowd shows our biggest advantage: we speak deep-tech fluently. We avoid generic, shallow tech templates. Instead, Studio 1947 delivers rigorous, data-faithful visual design that respects the intelligence of the scientific community. Every challenge interface, dataset callout and enterprise brand asset looks authoritative and inspiring, and ready to rally the world's finest algorithmic minds.

When deep-tech platforms, AI researchers and enterprise data teams look for a creative partner, they don't want a traditional graphic agency. They need someone who is comfortable with abstract maths, clear communication and interactive data visualisation. The task is big: take a complex, many-sided machine learning challenge and frame it so the world's best data scientists can grasp the problem at once, benchmark their models and push science forward.

Our work with AIcrowd is the longest technical design relationship in our company's history. Our CEO, Rabiul Islam, started it years ago, before Studio 1947 formally existed. It has grown into a strong working framework. Together we have shaped the visual identity and communication for world-defining AI challenges hosted with institutions like NeurIPS, Meta, Amazon and the KDD Cup.

_sourceSections.heading: The Core Triad: Science, Communication, Visualisation
body: To connect complex algorithms with human understanding, our workflow rests on three fixed pillars:

_sourceSections.label: Science
body: We get our team deep into the mechanics of each challenge, whether that is reinforcement learning, multi-modal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or clinical biomedical telemetry.

_sourceSections.label: Communication
body: We build clear information hierarchies and narrative frames that remove confusion, so developer communities around the world quickly understand scoring metrics and data parameters.

_sourceSections.label: Visualisation
body: We make high-fidelity key visuals, dynamic leaderboard assets and technical UI that turn dry mathematical formulas into rich, inspiring and useful design.

_sourceSections.heading: Phase 1: The Legacy Era
body: Before Studio 1947 was formally set up, our CEO Rabiul Islam laid the groundwork for this deep-tech design method. He led individual consulting tracks for AIcrowd's most important enterprise benchmarks.

_sourceSections.label: Amazon KDD Cup 2024
body: Benchmarking Large Language Models on how well they handle complex, multi-task digital commerce tasks (for example, personalised shopping tracking, understanding query intent and product recommendations).

We built a visual system that balanced Amazon's corporate identity with a refined network-graph look. The artwork mapped the layered tracks of LLMs parsing data strings. It turned dry e-commerce data into an inviting playground for NLP engineering talent worldwide.

media.alt: Amazon KDD Cup 2024 challenge key visual: network-graph artwork mapping multi-task LLM commerce tracks

_sourceSections.label: ADDI: Alzheimer's Detection Challenge
body: Using advanced data science pipelines to detect and track biomarkers for early-stage Alzheimer's disease in clinical medical trials.

Healthcare data needs absolute precision and real human empathy. We moved right away from cold, sterile tech patterns. Instead we made an organic, data-led composition focused on neural pathway connections and structural brain metrics. The interface put crisp, readable typographic grids first, for medical researchers scanning complex rules.

media.alt: ADDI Alzheimer's Detection Challenge key visual, organic neural pathway composition over a typographic grid

media.alt: SUADD '23 key visual: vector tracking grids, bounding boxes and depth heatmaps over an aerial landscape

_sourceSections.label: Data Purchasing Challenge 2022
body: Simulating automated algorithmic marketplaces where AI agents must evaluate, bid on and buy high-value datasets on a limited budget.

To ground an abstract marketplace, we built a sharp, structured system asset that echoed algorithmic trading floors. Clean geometric arrays and dark-mode data nodes gave the identity the feel of quantitative finance and data as a commodity.

media.alt: Data Purchasing Challenge 2022 key visual: geometric arrays and dark-mode data nodes evoking an algorithmic trading floor

_sourceSections.label: Multi-Agent Behavior Challenge 2022
body: Mapping, predicting and classifying the intricate social and physical paths of interacting multi-agent systems (for example, automated tracking of animal models in neuroscience, or multi-robot swarms).

We designed a complex choreography of motion lines. Using the brand's neon colour gradients, we traced crossing path arrays and emerging behavioural clusters. The key art showed how the science tracks each agent's intent within a busy, unified group.

media.alt: Multi-Agent Behavior Challenge 2022 key visual, intersecting neon motion trajectories forming behavioural clusters

_sourceSections.label: NeurIPS 2021: AWS DeepRacer: AI Driving Olympics Challenge
body: Advanced reinforcement learning models trained to drive scale-model autonomous vehicles around unpredictable, high-speed physical racing tracks.

We merged AWS corporate branding with the high-octane world of motorsport. The design system used sharp velocity lines, technical racing track grids and telemetry dashboard indicators. Together they capture the intense, micro-second optimisation that autonomous driving agents need.

media.alt: NeurIPS 2021 AWS DeepRacer key visual: velocity lines, racing track grids and telemetry indicators

_sourceSections.label: NeurIPS 2020: Procgen Competition
body: Testing how well AI agents' reinforcement learning generalises inside procedurally generated 2D game environments.

We paid homage to classic 8-bit and 16-bit retro developer environments, but lifted the look with clean, modular vector structure. The design showed how endless randomised game levels grow from a fixed set of underlying code rules. It spoke directly to the gaming and ML research crowd.

media.alt: NeurIPS 2020 Procgen Competition key visual: retro 8-bit game environments rebuilt as clean modular vector tiles
